author: ojiudezue
title: Restart cadence keeps the crossing ledger permanently unknown
summary: Every crossing ledger term for a week read applied=false reason=unknown. The ledger's state is RAM-only and resets on each HA restart; only a 15-minute empty-house anchor makes it known. One anchor fired in 3.5 days and the next deploy's restart erased it 8 minutes later. Known time was ~34 min in 3.5 days across ~13 restarts.
why: The ledger was designed assuming long uptimes; the arc's ship cadence (often 2 restarts a day) violates that silently, so the ledger, the planned interior floor and any ledger promotion produce nothing. Found only because a day audit asked why every term said 'unknown'.
alternatives_considered: Persist L and known across restart when the downtime gap had no door activity (verifiable from the recorder after boot)
A second anchor that does not need an empty house (operator dropped the checkpoint anchor 11-15 as fragile)
implications: The ledger floor (arc row 7) cannot be measured or built until known-time is fixed. Releases should batch to fewer restarts. Any RAM-only state machine in URA should be checked against the real restart rate (ties to RESTART-SAFETY-DOCTRINE-1).
